title: Late-arrival consumption imputer and confidence scoring pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We currently see a 3–7% recurring discrepancy in daily customer invoices that traces to out-of-order event arrival from the ingestion layer (s3 event lag, kinesis replays, late agent-side batching). Downstream billing jobs assume near-real-time arrival and can permanently attribute zero-cost for late tokens when a compact window has already closed. Goal: Build a standalone imputation pipeline that (1) detects late-arriving token/usage records, (2) computes an imputed contribution for the affected billing windows using probabilistic smoothing and source-aware heuristics, (3) assigns a confidence score per imputed record, and (4) surfaces corrections into the billing aggregator with idempotent backfill semantics and audit trails.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline identifies >99% of late-arrival events in synthetic testbench and labels them for imputation
Imputed token counts reduce day-over-day invoice variance attributable to late-arrivals by >=80% in the staging replay
Each imputed row contains a stable confidence_score in [0.0,1.0] and a provenance field (ingest_path, event_ts, observed_ts) persisted to the billing store
Roll-forward is idempotent: replays of the same late event do not double-apply credits or charges
Operational metrics and dashboards are available in Grafana; alerting fires if daily late-adjusted delta > 1% for a tenant
implementation_notes: Architecture: a streaming job (Flink/Beam) reads the raw ingestion topic (kinesis/s3-notifications), tags late events based on ingestion_timestamp vs event_timestamp windows, buffers short-tail lateness (<6h) for deterministic attribution and routes long-tail lateness (>6h and <72h) to the imputer job

Imputation model: lightweight Bayesian smoothing that combines tenant historical per-request token distribution, route-level priors, and same-day observed tokens; fallback to deterministic proportional allocation when confidence <0.3

Confidence scoring: features include lateness_seconds, tenant_token_variance, route_sparsity, is_replay_flag, source_quality_score; model implemented as logistic regression trained on previous 90-day labeled replays
State & idempotency: use a compact idempotency key (tenant+request_id+event_hash) and persistent checkpoints in the dedupe store (current ledger service) to prevent double application

Backfill & order: corrections are written to the billing_corrections topic with explicit correction_type (impute|replace|nullify) and correction_window; billing aggregator applies correction in a strict sequence with guaranteed exactly-once semantics
Data retention: imputed rows have a TTL of 540 days and are tagged for audit; raw late events are retained per existing ingestion policy
Privacy: imputation uses only aggregated token-level features and does not surface prompt contents; integrate KMS key for correction topic encryption
monitoring: Metrics to emit: late_event_rate{tenant,route}, imputed_token_count, imputation_confidence_histogram, correction_application_latency, duplicate_correction_attempts
Dashboards: billing->imputation overview with top-20 tenants by imputed delta, 7/30/90 day trend, and per-route breakdown
Alerts: P1 alert if daily applied corrections for any tenant exceed 2% of billed tokens or if duplicate_correction_attempts > 0 for more than 10 minutes
SLOs: 99.95% of imputation corrections applied within 10 minutes of detection for short-tail lateness; operational window for long-tail replays is 24 hours
rollout_plan: Phase 0: unit/integration tests + full replay of past 30 days in staging; validate imputed token delta against historical known replays
Phase 1: opt-in per-tenant in staging; cross-check applied corrections against manual audit for top 5 tenants
Phase 2: gradual production rollout (5 tenants -> 50 -> all), start with low-variance tenants; monitor cost exposure dashboard and pause if unexpected crediting occurs
Phase 3: default-on with guardrails (confidence threshold 0.25, correction caps per-tenant) and post-rollout audit for first 7 days
comments: 2026-03-01 Aisha Patel: Ticket created after billing ops postmortem (incident#2026-02-27). Initial design sketch attached in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BR/Late+Arrival+Imputation

2026-03-03 Ethan Gomez: Spiked Bayesian smoothing prototype in pyreplay; initial false-positive rate acceptable on synthetic dataset. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/replay-impute/pull/42

2026-03-06 Data Eng review: flagged the need for idempotency key size reduction; recommended using sha256(event) truncated to 64 bits and adding tenant salt. Also requested encryption-at-rest for correction topic.
2026-03-08 PM feedback (R. Liu): Add a manual override in Console to reject automated corrections for regulated tenants and surface a corrections preview before commit.

2026-03-10 Dev note: Implemented confidence_score and persisted provenance fields; end-to-end staging replay shows 86% reduction in variance for test tenants. Next: add Grafana dashboard panels and implement correction caps per tenant.
2026-03-12 Ops: scheduled a canary on production pipeline for 5 non-critical tenants on 2026-03-20; notifying support and finance teams to watch daily deltas.
